html:
The Battle of the Berezina was fought from 26 to 29 November 1812 near Barysaw in Belarus, as Napoleon's army, retreating from Moscow, crossed the Berezina River under Russian attack.

Russian armies were closing in from three sides and the bridge at Barysaw was burned. Dutch engineers of the Grande Armée, standing in icy water, built two pontoon bridges at Studzianka. Most of the fighting men got across, but when the bridges were burned behind them, thousands of stragglers and camp followers were left to die or be captured. The French invasion of Russia had begun with about 600,000 men; far fewer than 100,000 made it out. In French "Bérézina" still means a total disaster.
sum: The Battle of the Berezina was fought from 26 to 29 November 1812 near Barysaw in Belarus, as Napoleon's army, retreating from Moscow, crossed the Berezina River under Russian attack.
